section.title: Concavity and second derivatives
section.p: The first derivative tells whether a function is rising or falling. It does not tell the whole shape.
A car can move forward while speeding up. It can also move forward while slowing down. In both cases the velocity is positive, but the motion feels different.
Graphs have the same distinction. A graph can be increasing while bending upward, or increasing while bending downward. The second derivative measures that bending.

statement.p: A car can move forward while speeding up, or move forward while slowing down. In both cases velocity is positive. In your own words, why does the first derivative miss this distinction, and what extra question does the second derivative ask?

hint.p: f' tells whether the graph is rising or falling. f'' tells whether those slopes themselves are increasing or decreasing.

subsection.title: Concave up and concave down
subsection.p: The word concavity describes the direction a graph bends.
If the slopes are increasing as we move left to right, the graph is concave up. It bends like a cup.
If the slopes are decreasing as we move left to right, the graph is concave down. It bends like a cap.

note.title: Concavity
note.p: Suppose f is differentiable on an interval I.
The function f is concave up on I if f' is increasing on I.
The function f is concave down on I if f' is decreasing on I.

subsection.p: This definition says that concavity is really a statement about how the tangent slopes change.
Because the second derivative is the derivative of f', the first derivative sign rule applied to f' gives the main test.

subsection.title: Inflection points
subsection.p: A point where the concavity changes is called an inflection point.

note.title: Inflection point
note.p: A point (c,f(c)) on the graph of f is an inflection point if the concavity of f changes at c.

paragraphs.p: It means the test is silent. We must return to the first derivative test, the shape of the graph, or another argument.

subsection.title: Where this points
subsection.p: The first derivative tells where the graph rises and falls. The second derivative tells where the graph bends upward and downward.
Together, they give a much richer picture:

But a graph can also have asymptotes, holes, intercepts, and end behavior. The next step is to put all the evidence together into a graph-sketching method that is guided by calculus rather than by guesswork.
